title: Runtime anomaly catalog and service-health orthogonal view
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a unified "anomaly catalog" and a complementary orthogonal service-health view to help oncall and SRE quickly classify and triage inference incidents. This ticket defines the taxonomy, tracing hook changes, metric/log pipeline transforms, and a new dashboard layout that presents orthogonal slices (latency, quota/backpressure, model rejections, HTTP/gRPC codes) aligned with a deterministic incident playbook.

Goals:
- Produce a canonical anomaly catalog that maps observable signals to probable root causes (timeouts, overload, KV/cache pressure, model OOMs, generation rejections, HTTP 4xx/5xx flavors, gRPC status codes).
- Implement lightweight tracing hooks that annotate spans with categorical failure tags at the ingress, runtime, and egress layers.
- Update metrics/log ingestion pipelines to emit normalized fields (failure_type, overload_signal, model_error_code, rpc_status_family).
- Build a service-health orthogonal dashboard (multi-panel) that surfaces correlated slices with drilldowns into traces and raw logs.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire alerting stack. We will integrate with existing SLO alerts but not change thresholds here.
- Replacing model-level instrumentation (follow-up work will be issued with model teams).

Acceptance criteria:
- Canonical catalog documented in Confluence with mapping for >= 12 observed signal patterns and recommended triage steps.
- Tracing hook PR merged to runtime that adds 3 new span attributes: failure_category, backpressure_level, model_rejection_tag.
- Pipeline transforms added to the ingestion layer: normalize failure_category and expose as labels in metrics index and log parsing rules.
- Dashboard deployed in Console staging with panels: (1) failure_category heatmap by route, (2) latency/90/99 foldover with correlated error rate, (3) overload signature timeseries (CPU/GPU/memory + queue length), (4) model_error code breakdown with sample traces.
- Drilldown from dashboard panel into trace timeline links and the representative log bundle for at least 3 example incidents.

Design notes / taxonomy (first pass):
- failure_category values: timeout_client, timeout_model_kv, overload_queue, overload_gpu_mem, model_rejection_bad_input, model_rejection_internal, rpc_4xx_client, rpc_5xx_server, resource_limit_oom, circuit_breaker_invoked
- overload_signal heuristic: (queue_depth > 50 && avg_service_time > baseline*1.3) OR (gpu_util > 92% && backend_pending_requests > 0)
- model_error_code: preserve model-specific enums but map to model_error_internal/model_error_user/model_error_resource for dashboard aggregation
- rpc_status_family: map gRPC codes into families (OK, CLIENT_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) and expose both numeric and family label

Tracing hook changes (runtime):
- On request ingress, attach request_origin and expected_latency_sla.
- At dispatch, if queue_delay > X ms annotate span.backpressure_level = "high" and failure_category = "overload_queue" on subsequent error spans.
- On model return, if model returns structured rejection -> set model_rejection_tag with rejection_reason and map to higher-level failure_category.

Metrics/log pipeline changes (observability infra):
- Add `failure_category` as a normalized field in the log-parsing stage (Logstash/FluentD config snippet included in Confluence).
- Emit aggregated metrics: telemetry.failure_category.count (labels: route, model_family, region), telemetry.model_error.code_count, telemetry.rpc_status.family_count.
- Ensure these metrics are low-cardinality by mapping model-specific codes to families in the transform.

Dashboard layout (Console staging):
- Top row: service-health snapshot (OK/Degraded/Down) + global error budget usage.
- Middle row: orthogonal panes (failure_category heatmap; rpc_status_family distribution; model_error family timeseries).
- Bottom row: investigative panels (sample trace list; recent incident bundles; correlated infra metrics).
- Each panel contains a pre-built query and a "Open trace" link that includes trace_id and a minimal context cookie for the trace viewer.

Query samples (Prometheus/Influx/ES style examples to be used by dashboard):
- telemetry.failure_category.count{route=~"/v1/.*"} by (failure_category)
- sum(rate(telemetry.rpc_status.family_count[5m])) by (rpc_family, route)
- topk(10, sum(rate(telemetry.model_error.code_count[5m])) by (model_error_family))

Implementation plan:
1) Finalize taxonomy doc (this ticket). 2) Runtime tracing hook prototype (PR to runtime repo) - feature-flagged. 3) Pipeline transforms in staging (log parsing + metric mappers). 4) Dashboard panels assembled in Console staging and QA by oncall rotation. 5) Canary release to a subset of traffic, monitor SLI regressions for 48h. 6) Full rollout and retro.

Rollback plan:
- Disable tracing hook flag and revert pipeline transform mapping if we observe >5% metric ingestion errors or unacceptable increase in storage costs.

Risks:
- Cardinality explosion from model-specific codes (mitigated via family mapping).
- Slight added latency from tracing hook serialization (hooks are lightweight; feature-flagged).
- Misclassification due to heuristic thresholds; will iterate after 2 weeks of data.

Notes:
- We will run a 2-week observational period in staging to validate taxonomy mapping thresholds before canary.
- If we detect model-specific high variance, we'll issue follow-ups for per-model instrumentation work and bump customer_impact to high if customer-facing error exposure increases.
